sections.skill: Give each person their own login and only the access they need

questions.prompt: What does least privilege mean?

choices.text: Giving only the access a person needs for their job
Giving the owner the least access
Giving everyone full access to everything in the business

questions.correct_answer: Giving only the access a person needs for their job
questions.intro: Give each person their OWN login rather than sharing one password, and give only the ACCESS they need for their job (called least privilege): a helper who packs orders may need the order list, not the bank account. Keep a list of who has access to what. The owner should hold the main (administrator) account for key services. When someone leaves or changes roles, remove or change their access the same day.

questions.prompt: Why give each person their own login?

choices.text: It makes passwords easier to share
It is required for free accounts only, not paid
Access can be tracked and removed individually

questions.prompt: The cleaner's keys are like what?

choices.text: Access only to what the job needs
A master key to every single room

questions.correct_answer: Access only to what the job needs
questions.intro: In an office building, a cleaner may have keys to the hallways and the kitchen but not the safe. The manager has the master key. Each person signs for their own keys, and when someone leaves, their keys are returned the same day. Business accounts work the same way: separate keys, only the rooms each person needs, and a master key the owner keeps.
